claim: In the ideal Glover–Balmer stream-depletion model, a constant-rate pumping pulse of duration \(\tau>0\) has a unique global maximum normalized stream-depletion rate at time \(t_*\) after pumping begins, with \(t_* > \max\{\tau,2a/3\}\), \(t_* < \tau+2a/3\), where \(a=d^2S/(4T)\); moreover \(dt_*/d\tau\in(0,1)\), so the peak time rises less than one-for-one with pulse duration.

correctness.rationale: Differentiation gives q(t)=sqrt(a)/(sqrt(pi)t^(3/2)) exp(-a/t). For the finite pulse, the derivative after shutdown is q(t)-q(t-tau). The logarithm of the ratio has derivative with a quadratic sign factor, producing exactly one zero and hence one maximum. The mode of q is 2a/3, giving the strict bracket; implicit differentiation gives 0<dt*/dtau<1.

value.rationale: Maximum stream depletion is a natural water-management quantity because stream impacts may peak after pumping ceases. The exact strict bracket and the derivative bound convert this qualitative issue into a parameter-explicit monitoring-window and pulse-duration comparison for the classical model, rather than merely recomputing a tabulated response.
